0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 November 1985, after the draft finalized by the Cordage Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 0.2 Originally this standard was based on IND/TC/2147(d) `Rope, jute, hawser-laid and IND/TC/2146(b) `Line, jute, hawser-laid'. Based on the experience of the Ministry of Defence in the use of this specification, the Controllerate of Inspection Textiles and Clothing, Kanpur proposed a downward revision of breaking load values to the extent of 15 percent. Accordingly, in this standard the breaking load values have been modified. Opportunity has also been availed to introduce tolerances for rope dia and to amend sampling clause and some other clauses in the standard. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with The number of significant places retained in the rounded IS : 2-1960*. off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS : 5177 - 1985 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, 1984* shall apply. 3. ATMOSPHERIC TESTING CONDITIONS the definitions as given in IS : 3871FOR CONDITIONING AND

3.1 The tests shall normally be carried out under prevailing atmospheric conditions. In all cases of dispute, however, tests shall be carried out on samples which have been conditioned for 24 hours in an atmosphere at 65 f 2 percent relative humidity and 27 f 2�C temperature ( see IS : 6359-1971t ). Where practicable, tests shall be made in the standard conditioning atmosphere; otherwise, they shall be made as quickly as possible but not exceeding 15 minutes of removal of the test pieces from the conditioning atmosphere. 4. MANUFACTURE 4.1 Yarn - The yarns used for the manufacture of all sizes of lines and ropes shall be 3-ply jute yarn of 275 tex x 3 ( 8 grist x 3 ). The number of yarns in each strand of line or rope shall be in accordance with Table 1 and each strand shall contain equal number of yarns. 4.2 Strand - The strands of line or rope shall be well formed, evenly twisted and shall be free from grooves and sunken yarns. 4.3 Line and Rope 4.3.1 Line - The line should be well and evenly laid and should be free from defects. The finished strand shall have Z-lay. The lines should be firm in lay and satisfactory in handle. The lines should not be too stiff in handle or too loose ( that is, lines in which the strands can be readily untwisted by hand ). The lines shall be supplied in coils/hanks and each coil/hank shall be continuous throughout its length and shall not contain splices or joins in the strands or in the line.
4.3.2 Rope - The rope shall be well and evenly laid and should be free from defects. The finished rope shall have Z-lay. The number of turns per metre should be such that the product of the turns per metre and the diameter in millimetre shall be 266. The deviation from this number either way may be permitted if the lay and handle of the rope are satisfactory. The rope should be firm in lay and satisfactory in The rope should not be too stiff in handle or too loose ( that is, handle. *Glossary of terms relating to fibre ropes and cordages ( jrst n&ion TMethod for conditioning of textiler.

IS : 5177 - 1985 4.4 Lubrication - Weighting or loading material shall not be used. For the purpose of dressing the fibre, an emulsion or a mixture of oil and grease shall be added so that the amount of dressing applied to the fibre when determined by extraction with petroleum ether or other suitable solvent, be not less than 5 nor more than 15 percent calculated on the basis of the weight of the finished line or rope. 4.5 Rot-Proofing Treatment - If so ordered, ropes and lines shall be For ropes treated with rot-proofed with zinc or copper naphthanate. zinc napthanate the zinc content shall be between 0.8 and 1.2 percent and for ropes treated with copper naphthanate the copper content shall be between 0.4 and 0.8 percent when tested in accordance with IS : 3522 ( Part 1 )-1966*. The rot-proofing agent may be used in place of, or in conjunctron with, the lubricant ( See 4.4 ) normally used for the purpose of dressing the fibre. Ropes or lines which have been SO treated shall otherwise comply in all respects with the requirements of this standard. 5. REQUIREMENTS 5.1 Mass - The gross mass of a lot of lines or ropes when determined according to the method given in IS : 7071 ( Part 2 )-1974t shall be as agreed to between the buyer and the seller, or as entered in the despatch note subject to a tolerance of f 3.5 percent. The mass of the packing material should not be more than 1.5 percent of the gross mass of lines or ropes. 5.2 Length - The length of each coil of rope shall be 220 m and the length of each coil/hank of lines shall be 37 m unless otherwise agreed to between the buyer and the seller. The length of the coil shall be determined by the method given in IS : 7071 ( Part 2 )-1974t. 5.3 Other Requirements the requirements of Table 1. 6. PACKING 6.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the buyer and the seller, lines and ropes shall be packed in accordance with IS : 3256-1980$. 7. MARKING 7.1 Each coil shall have a label attached on which shall be legibly and indelibly marked the following: -_ a) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark; the The jute lines and ropes shall conform to

The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality IS1 control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. checked by IS1 for conformity to that marked products are also continuously Details of conditions under which a licence for the standard as a further safeguard. use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

8. SAMPLING 8.1 Lot - The number diameter manufactured buyer against a despatch of coils/hanks of rope/line of the same nominal under similar conditions and delivered to a note shall constitute a lot. of at

8.2 Sample Size - Sampling shall be as representative as possible the lot subjected to the measurements and tests. Draw the samples random, at the rate shown by the following formula: S = 0'4

N Jwhere S is the number of lengths of rope/line and X is the size of the lot expressed as a number of coils/hanks. When S as calculated is not a whole number, round off the value obtained to give a whole number in accordance with the procedure laid down in IS : 2-1960*. In case where S is less than 1, draw one sample length.

APPENDIX
( Table METHODS A-l. BREAKING OF TEST LOAD

A

1)
LOAD of appropriate head of not less

FOR BREAKING

A-l.1 Apparatus - Rope tensile testing machine capacity with constant-rate-of traverse of the straining than 150 mm/minute or greater than 305 mm/minute.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ),

7

Is; : 5177 - 1985

A-l.2 Procedure
A-1.2.1 With Ordinary Grifs - Mount each specimen with an initial length of not less than one metre between the grips of the testing machine. Apply gradually and continuously increasing load until the specimen breaks. If fracture occurs at or near the grips at less than the specified breaking load, disregard the test and take a further test. Accept the test results corresponding to any specimen that fractures through causes attributable to grip damage as meeting the requirements of the specification provided that the load recorded is not less than 95 percent of the minimum specified breaking load. A-1.2.2 With Ballard Grips - Small size ropes may be tested on testing machine with bollard grips. In such cases, mount the test specimen with an initial length of not less than 250 mm between the bollards of the testing machine ensuring that rate of traverse of the straining head for constant-rate-of-traverse machine is as near as possible numerically equal in mm per minute to the length of the specimen. Apply gradually and continuously increasing load until the specimen breaks. If fracture occurs at or near the grips at less than the specified breaking load, disregard the test and take a further test. Accept the test result corresponding to any specimen that fractures through causes attributable to grip damage as meeting the requirements of this specification provided that the load recorded is not less than 95 percent of the minimum specified breaking load. A-1.2.3 With Ram Horn Grips - Mount each specimen with an initial length of not less than 1 metre between two ram horn grips fixed at both the moving and stationary ends of the constant rate of traverse testing machine, taking care that the rope does not slip from the grips Apply gradually and continuously increasing load until during testing. the specimen breaks. Record the load indicated by the machine. If fracture occurs at or near the grips at less than specified breaking load, disregard the test and take a further test. A-1.2.4 Eye-Spliced Rope Test - Ropes with the ends eye-spliced may be used for the purpose of testing the tensile strength of the rope. The diameter of testing bollards shall not be less than 100 mm when testing ropes up to and including 40 mm nominal diameter and not less than 150 mm diameter for ropes larger than 40 mm diameter. In order to obtain a true value of rope strength, it is desirable that there be as great a length of rope as possible between the splices. When tested eyespliced, the rope shall be deemed to conform to the requirements of this specification provided the breaking load obtained from the specimen is not less than 90 percent of the breaking load given in Table 1 and provided that the fracture occurs at the splice. 8
